settings.title: Settings
settings.accountWhy: Keep your projects online as well as here, so they open on your other devices, and let Motiff Lab's server read sheet music and recordings for you.
settings.signInHow: No password: each time, a code comes to your email.
settings.scanWhat: Motiff Lab reads the notes from a PDF or photo of printed music, and writes down the notes it hears in an audio or video recording. It asks before each send.

settings.scanDocker: Run these with Docker in a copy of the Motiff Lab repository. The build takes a few minutes and downloads about 2 GB once; after that the server works offline.
settings.scanBadAddress: Give an address such as http://localhost:8765, with no path after it.

settings.scanElsewhere: This address is another computer, so pages and recordings you send leave this one. Each send asks first.

transcribe.heading: Transcribe a recording
transcribe.setUp: Motiff Lab can write down the notes it hears in an audio or video recording of piano music, with the same scan server as scanning.
transcribe.setUpLink: Set up the scan server in Settings
transcribe.what: This browser takes the sound out of the recording, so a video's picture stays on this device, and sends the first 2½ minutes of sound to the scan server at {0}, which writes down the notes it hears and then deletes the sound. If this browser cannot read the file, the file itself is sent. The notes are a first draft, marked as detected for you to check by ear.
transcribe.sendHosted: Send the sound to Motiff Lab's scan server, which deletes it once heard
transcribe.sendElsewhere: Send the sound to {0}, which is another computer
transcribe.choose: Choose an audio or video recording to transcribe
transcribe.drop: Drop a recording here, or click to choose one
transcribe.busy: Listening… this takes a few seconds for each minute of sound
transcribe.heard: {0} s of the recording heard in {1} s, sending included.
transcribe.draft: Every note is marked as detected: it is what the engine heard, which misses the pedal and can mistake an overtone for a note.
transcribe.cut: Only the first 2½ minutes were heard. Transcribe a shorter passage to get the rest.
transcribe.barsOn: Write the notes in bars worked out from the playing
transcribe.barsFound: {0} with a quarter at {1} a minute. This is worked out from the notes: the beat their onsets fit best, with bar lines where the bass falls. The notes do not move and still sound as recorded.
transcribe.barsPickup: The piece starts with a pickup.
transcribe.shortBars.one: {0} bar is cut short where the downbeat moves, for example at a repeat.
transcribe.shortBars.many: {0} bars are cut short where the downbeat moves, for example at a repeat.
transcribe.barsOff: The notes stay in the bars the engine wrote: 4/4 at 120 beats a minute, which may not line up with the music.
transcribe.barsNone: The notes follow no steady beat Motiff Lab could find, so they stay in the bars the engine wrote: 4/4 at 120 beats a minute.
transcribe.tempoHow: If the notes look twice as fast or slow as in print, change the tempo: shorter notes become longer, or the other way round.
transcribe.barsFollow: The tempo follows the playing: the beat slows down and speeds up with the recording, so the number is a typical quarter.
transcribe.shiftHow: If the first beat of each bar sits elsewhere than in print, move the bar lines by a beat.
transcribe.tooLarge: This browser cannot take the sound out of this file, and the file is larger than the 50 MB that can be sent as it is.
transcribe.tooLargeTip: Record audio only, or a shorter passage: M4A or MP3 from a phone works well.
transcribe.notHeardTip: Record closer to the piano, with less noise around it.
transcribe.off: Transcription is off. Give the scan server's address in Settings.
transcribe.signIn: Sign in on Settings to transcribe with Motiff Lab's scan server.
transcribe.oldServer: This scan server cannot transcribe yet. Build and start it again from the latest Motiff Lab (see Settings).
transcribe.failed: The scan server could not transcribe this recording.
transcribe.tooLong: The scan server took too long to answer.

import.scanSetUp: Motiff Lab can read a PDF or a photo of printed music with a scan server.
import.scanWhat: A PDF of up to 8 pages, or a photo of one page, is sent to the scan server at {0} to be read, and deleted there as soon as it has been. A page takes 20 to 60 seconds. The notes come back marked as detected, for you to check.
import.scanWhatHere: A PDF of up to 8 pages, or a photo of one page, is sent to the scan server at {0} on this computer to be read, and deleted there as soon as it has been. A page takes 20 to 60 seconds. The notes come back marked as detected, for you to check.

import.scanDrop: Drop a PDF or photo here, or click to choose one
import.scanTooLarge: This file is larger than 50 MB, the most the scan server reads.
import.scanTooLargeTip: Scan fewer pages at a time, or save the photo at a lower resolution.
import.scanNotReadTip: Try a sharper photo that shows the whole page, straight on and in good light.

import.goRecording: Write down its notes with Notes from a recording
import.scanRead: {0} read in {1} s by the scan server.
import.scanFlagged: {0} of {1} may have been misread. Every note is marked as detected until you check it; after opening, the Scan tab in the workspace takes you to each of these bars.
import.scanClean: No bar looks wrong to the checks. The notes are still a reading of the page, marked as detected until you check them.
import.readHere: Read in {0} s on this device.
import.roundedHow: Rounded timing moves a note by at most half a tick, 1/960 of a quarter note.
import.notRounded: No timing had to be rounded.
import.noRestoreYet: Restore rhythm is not in this version yet, so for now the file plays as it was recorded.
import.warningKinds: Assumed: the file did not say, so Motiff Lab chose a value. Repaired: the file was damaged and Motiff Lab kept what it could read. Left out: not used in this version.
import.handsInferredWhy: Hands were worked out from pitch and movement, not read from the file.
import.openSaves: Opening saves the piece as a project, so you can come back to it.

explore.buildOn: Build on it in the Tools tab.
explore.leaveHint: Go back to what you had before this experiment.

tools.ownChoiceHint: Your own choice of what to keep.
tools.ownChoice: Your own choice of what to keep
tools.whatToKeepHint: Properties the variation should leave as they are. A chip turns dashed when the step changes it.
tools.scopeHint: Rhythm reshape and Articulation can change one layer and leave the rest as it is. The melody is the top line of the notes, whichever hand plays it.
tools.wholeSelection: Changes every selected note, whatever Change says.
tools.acceptHint: Keep this step; the next change builds on it.
tools.rejectHint: Drop this step and go back to the accepted ones.
tools.undoHint: Take back the last accepted step.
tools.redoHint: Bring back the last step you undid.
tools.pickChange: Pick a change to hear it. Keep marks what should stay the same, and a change that would alter a kept property is not offered. The original notes are never changed.
tools.exportMotifHint: Save the selected notes as a MIDI file for a DAW: one track per hand, with the tempo.
tools.exportVariationHint: Save the variation as a MIDI file for a DAW: one track per hand, with the tempo.
tools.selectFirst: Select some bars on the roll first: drag across it, or click a bar number. Then pick what to keep and a change here.
edit.label: Edit variation notes
edit.hint: Change, add or remove notes of the variation you hear; with no steps yet, this makes a variation by hand. Each edit is a step: Undo takes it back, and a Keep chip turns dashed when an edit changes what it keeps. The original notes are never changed.
notes.addAfterHint: Add a note of the same pitch and length straight after this one.
notes.removeFromVariationHint: Take this note out of the variation.
notes.removeFromPieceHint: Take this note out of the piece.
notes.revertHint: Put this note back as it was imported.
correct.label: Correct notes
correct.hint: Fix what the import got wrong in the selected notes. Corrected notes are marked as edited by you; Undo or Revert puts the imported value back exactly.
correct.selectFirst: Select some bars to list their notes here.
correct.removed: Removed: {0}. Revert brings a note back:
second.label: Second file and tracks
second.toggle: Compare with a second file, mute and solo tracks
second.hint: Compare the piece with another file, such as your own variation of it.
op.V1.question: How to reshape the rhythm
op.syncopate.hint: Notes on a beat start half a beat early and are held into the beat.
op.dotted.hint: Pairs of notes a quarter, an eighth or a 16th apart become long–short.
op.halfTime.hint: Every note twice as long, and twice as far from the start of the selection.
op.doubleTime.hint: Every note half as long, and half as far from the start of the selection.
op.later1.hint: Every note starts an eighth later; lengths stay.
op.later2.hint: Every note starts a quarter later; lengths stay.
op.later3.hint: Every note starts three eighths later; lengths stay.
op.V13.question: How long the notes sound
op.short.hint: Each note sounds for about a quarter of the time to the next one; pitches and onsets stay.
op.detached.hint: Each note sounds for about half of the time to the next one; pitches and onsets stay.
op.connected.hint: Each note holds until the next one starts; pitches and onsets stay.
op.V2.question: How the accompaniment plays its notes
op.heldChord.hint: Each bar's accompaniment notes, struck together once and held to the end of the bar.
op.repeatedChord.hint: Each bar's accompaniment notes, struck together on every eighth.
op.arpeggioUp.hint: One accompaniment note per 16th, from the lowest to the highest, then again.
op.arpeggioDown.hint: One accompaniment note per 16th, from the highest to the lowest, then again.
op.upDown.hint: One accompaniment note per triplet eighth, up to the highest and back down.
op.alberti.hint: Lowest, highest, middle, highest, one per 16th. Needs three different notes in each bar.
op.V4.question: Where the copies go
op.stepHigher.hint: A copy of the motif follows straight after, one scale step higher.
op.stepLower.hint: A copy of the motif follows straight after, one scale step lower.
op.climbing.hint: Three copies follow, each one scale step higher than the one before.
op.thirdLower.hint: A copy of the motif follows straight after, two scale steps lower.
op.V9.question: How the steps of the melody change
op.wider.hint: Each step of the melody grows by a scale step; the rhythm and the contour stay.
op.muchWider.hint: Each step of the melody grows by two scale steps; the rhythm and the contour stay.
op.narrower.hint: Each step of the melody shrinks by a scale step; the rhythm and the contour stay.
op.V10.question: How the melody turns
op.upsideDown.hint: The melody moves the other way from its first note, in scale steps of the key.
op.upsideDownExact.hint: The melody moves the other way from its first note, by the same number of semitones.
tools.notKept: No longer kept in the variation.
tools.notChecked: Not checked yet: this needs chord analysis.

compare.nothingAsked: Nothing was asked to be kept.
compare.nothing: No note changed pitch, start or length ({0}).
compare.originalHint: Hear the original phrase and show it in the score. The variation stays to come back to.
compare.variationHint: Hear the variation and show it in the score with the variation in place.
compare.alternateHint: Loops the original phrase, then the variation, then again.
